newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays firm vs dollar after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays firm vs dollar after choppy session.

text.p: The ringgit stayed firm against the dollar after a choppy Asian session with Bank Negara said to be capping the dollar at 2.5050, dealers said.
Profit-taking and fresh offshore and local bids for the dollar limited the ringgit's rise to 2.4950, they said.
"Negara was heard to have placed orders with agent banks to sell dollar/ringgit at 2.5050. So this level is likely to be the cap," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
Bank Negara was said to have intervened strongly in the market on Tuesday, spending an estimated $1.0 billion to help the ringgit.
The central bank again sold the dollar early on Wednesday, which sent dollar/ringgit down to a low of 2.4950, the ringgit's highest level since May 20.
Dealers said warning by Bank Negara that it would take stern steps to curb speculation in the ringgit did not have much immediate impact on dollar/ringgit.
Bank Negara Governor Ahmad Mohamed Don said on Wednesday that there would be no hesitation to introduce measures, including increasing interest rates, to curb speculation.
"Surprisingly the ringgit did not move much after the news. We had expected Bank Negara to come out with other actions apart from its intervention," said a dealer with a large Malaysian bank.
But the dollar will be pressured by the statement, he said.
Some dealers said the central bank's warning was necessary as speculators were waiting to hit the ringgit.
Ahmad confirmed intervention by Bank Negara to defend the ringgit, but declined to give the amount of its dollar sales.
He said the central bank had sufficient reserves to meet such intervention.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was quoted at 2.5033/43 to a dollar. It closed at 2.5070/90 in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.
